kelly_cs: Heads-up: customer kickoff at 09:00 PT. They asked for a one-page "Pocket Guide" for ops that their infra team can use during day0-7. Needs prefill, tenant-shard warmup tips, safe batching defaults, KV cache advice, streaming hygiene, quick validation commands, and a 72h renewal-risk watchlist. Keep it non-technical and copy/pasteable.

omar_se: I'll draft the pocket guide. Short bullets + copyable snippets. No internal-only flags.

viv_sre: Add a simple degraded run we can call out in bold so ops can act without waiting on support. Also include what to capture for fast correlation.

brynn_support: I'll paste top-5 real customer questions and one-line answers from recent tickets.

nate_pm: Suggest a tiny note about multi-tenant priming: prefilling per-tenant shard is better than global flood for large customers.

omar_se: Draft below (one continuous doc we can hand to ops):

kelly_cs: Pocket Guide 0 Ops Handback (1 page)
- Goal: stabilize performance & spend during pilot (day0-7). Catch regressions quickly and provide ops with clear, safe knobs.
- Tenant-shard prefill: prefill ~10-15% of active users per tenant shard (jitter start times) rather than flooding all tenants at once. This keeps cold-start risk low and gives meaningful prefix cache hit samples.
- Prefill snippet (copy/paste):
```bash
# tenant-shard prefill loop (example)
for tenant in tenant_list.txt; do
  for i in $(seq 1 50); do
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \n      -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n      -d '{"prompt":"welcome","max_tokens":64,"metadata":{"prefill":true,"tenant":"'$tenant'"}}' &
  done;
  sleep 2
done; wait
```
- Batching (safe defaults, hosted + dedicated):
  * Short prompts (<80 tokens): target_batch_size=18-28, max_batch_wait_ms=20-30.
  * Long outputs (>512 tokens): target_batch_size=3-6, max_batch_wait_ms=5-15 (avoid extra delay on long generations).
  * Tip: start conservative (smaller batch size) and increase if latency is stable.
- KV cache guidance: enable prefix_cache=true. Suggested TTLs: interactive sessions -> 300s; high-churn flows -> 30-60s. For multi-tenant flows, shard cache keys by tenant id to avoid cross-tenant pollution.
- Streaming hygiene: enable streaming for user-facing long outputs (>512 tokens). Recommended: keepalive_seconds=12, socket_timeout_ms=45000. Ensure proxies/load-balancers allow long-lived connections and do not buffer responses.
- Cost guards: set daily_token_limit + per_minute_cap for pilots. Add an alert webhook at 60% and a hard guard at 90% of the daily limit.
- Quick validation commands (copy/paste):
  * Check prefix cache hit rate: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://api.redwood.com/v1/metrics?name=prefix_cache_hit_rate"
  * Warm vs cold median latency: run 30 warm requests and 30 cold requests and compare median latencies in Console. Warm median should be significantly lower (~40-70% of cold).
  * Verify alerts: run a small simulated token burn against staging to confirm webhook fires.
- Degraded flow (do these in order if P95 tail rises for 30+min):
  1) Failover region: switch routing to alternate region with spare capacity via Console routing policy.
  2) Throttle & tighten: set per-client_rate_limit=100 req/min and reduce daily_token_limit temporarily.
  3) Reduce generation: lower max_generation_tokens by ~25% and reduce target_batch_size by 30%.
  4) Enable compact fallback model (labelled in Console as "compact fallback").
  5) If problems persist after these steps, open cs:urgent-review with sample requests and metrics.
- What to include for fast support triage: sample request JSON, route.name, account_id, tenant_id, prompt_hash, X-Request-ID, approximate timestamps, and whether request was prefilling/warm.
- 72h watchlist (renewal-risk signals):
  * tokens/day > baseline * 1.4 for 24+ hours;
  * P95 latency > SLO for 2+ hours;
  * sustained 5xx rate > 1% for 30+ minutes;
  If two of these trigger within 72h, tag the support ticket cs:renewal-risk and CS will convene a config audit + temporary protections.
- Short FAQ (1-line answers):
  Q: Tokens spiked after integration? -> Usually repeated full prompts or verbose per-request system text; enable client dedupe and targeted prefill.
  Q: Warm pools not improving latency? -> Check prefix_cache_hit_rate and confirm prefill volume per tenant shard.
  Q: Streaming stalls on mobile? -> Increase keepalive and confirm proxies/LBs allow long-lived connections (no buffering).
  Q: How to cap spend during pilot? -> Use daily_token_limit + per_minute_cap and webhook alerts at 60%.
  Q: What telemetry helps triage fastest? -> X-Request-ID, route.name, tenant_id, prompt_hash.

brynn_support: Nice. Adding real quick: most customers see prefix_cache_hit_rate climb to 30-50% within 10-30 minutes of correct prefill; call that out for expectations.

nate_pm: Callout for multi-tenant customers: stagger prefill across tenant shards by 10-20s to avoid concentrated bursts on the routing layer.
